title: Higher-Dimensional Riesz Transforms and Uniform Rectifiability
exact_target: Let $0<n<d$ be integers with $n\neq d-1$, and let $E\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be $n$-Ahlfors regular. If its $n$-dimensional Riesz transforms are bounded on $L^2(E)$, must $E$ be uniformly $n$-rectifiable? Ahlfors regularity means that its $n$-dimensional measure in balls is comparable to the $n$th power of their radius; uniform rectifiability requires quantitative large pieces of Lipschitz images.
